newsitem.title: LATVIA: MINISTRY UTS BUDGET INFLATION COMPENSATION.
newsitem.headline: MINISTRY UTS BUDGET INFLATION COMPENSATION.

text.p: The finance ministry on Thursday said it has cut the amount that it will compensate state insitutitions for inflation in 1998 to three percent from five after parliament approved spending increases in the 1997 budget.
Compensating for inflation effectively means that the expenditures of the institution are increased by the expected inflation amount.
It said the decision came after parliament voted on June 19 to increase spending by eight million lats in this year's budget.
"The finance ministry has informed institutions which are funded from the budget that the planned five percent inflation coefficient is no longer possible," the ministry said in a statement.
